answer.rationale: The write-path latency began climbing shortly after a release, making rollback the most direct candidate to test causal linkage before committing to a broader systemic fix. memory_b1 supports that rollbacks have cleanly resolved similar write-path degradations without customer impact, but I want to verify the original conditions (was it also under peak load, was latency multi-factor) since our current situation compounds a release with simultaneous settlement peak traffic, unlike the archived case. memory_b3 is checked because if headroom provisioning was the decisive factor in past peak-related latency issues, add_capacity might be safer than a rollback that could disrupt in-flight settlement writes during the peak window. Given the primary objective is preserving customer writes, a rollback risks losing in-flight transactional state if not handled carefully, so I flag downstream value risk explicitly. I am not fully certain the release is the root cause versus peak load alone, so I preserve that uncertainty and would re-evaluate quickly if latency doesn't recover post-rollback within the next window.
